itens.titulo: Broadcom CEO Hock Tan Echoes Warren Buffett in Warning About "Casino"-Like Investing
itens.descricao: Broadcom CEO Hock Tan Echoes Warren Buffett in Warning About "Casino"-Like Investing Yahoo Finance
trechos: Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005.
But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase.
"Act 2" is the global rollout.

"A lot of investors have no clue what they are investing in," he said, according to Bloomberg, and they "set very extreme expectations only to find out that it's almost like they are in a casino." Here's why they're concerned, and what you can do today.

There's a buoyant feeling about the future of the technology, but spending is reaching $1 trillion according to many estimates, and the confidence is based on expected earnings that don't exist today.
Tan noted that OpenAI has a $50 billion run rate, which would seem to be a viable business, but it hasn't figured out how to turn that into earnings.
"When you are a kid, you go to a video arcade, you play.
Your parents give you $10 of tokens, you finish it in 10 minutes, and you haven't learned anything," Tan noted.

itens.titulo: I’m Simply Not Worried About Broadcom’s Multi-Segment Drag
itens.descricao: I’m Simply Not Worried About Broadcom’s Multi-Segment Drag Yahoo Finance
trechos: Quick Read - Broadcom's AI revenue surged 221% to $16.7B, with management targeting $30+ EPS by fiscal 2028 while software's 94% gross margins fund a 15-year dividend streak.
- NVDA trades at 45x earnings and AMD at 215x with no dividend, while Broadcom's CEO claims its custom chips run advanced workloads at half the GPU cost.
Shares fell 8.04% in a week to $346.25 as chip stocks wobbled.
That leaves the stock up just 0.59% year to date, even though the business just reported the best quarter in its history.
Software Growth Looks Slow Only When You Stand It Next to AI In fiscal Q3, Semiconductor Solutions revenue rose 127% while Infrastructure Software grew 29%.
Non-AI chip revenue grew just 5% to $4.2 billion.
Now look at what the software side makes: a 94% gross margin and an operating margin near 84%, up 650 basis points from a year earlier.
Annual recurring revenue (ARR) grew 15%.
